related.title: Nvidia is done with Jensen Huang. The fallout in Washington is just beginning

cards.body: Jensen Huang is out at Nvidia. Washington is just getting started with him and the company he co-founded. Huang, the leather-jacket-clad CEO of the world's most important chipmaker, resigned from Nvidia on Thursday after revelations that he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. But the spy saga is gripping Washington, and lawmakers are preparing for investigations into how the now-ex-CEO's affair may have damaged U.S. artificial intelligence dominance, the national security implications and the executive's close relationship with President Donald Trump and his Cabinet. Republicans will have their chance first during their last six weeks controlling both chambers of Congress. GOP leaders immediately summoned Huang to Capitol Hill and said they would subpoena him if he doesn't agree to show up. In January, Democrats, who are already eager to make their mark with oversight when they take over the U.S. House and Senate, will be in the driver's seat. "In this environment where there's some really high stakes when it comes to our national security, I would expect there would be some follow-up, yeah," Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., told reporters at the Capitol on Thursday. Huang and the woman with whom he reportedly had a relationship, Alice Huang, an executive at the Singaporean technology company Megaspeed and an alleged Chinese spy have drawn congressional attention. And Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has drawn fire after reports this week that he stalled President Donald Trump's crackdowns on firms routing Nvidia chips to China. Some Congress members have also called for an investigation into the role of the Bureau of Industry and Security, a subagency of the Commerce Department that manages and enforces export controls, in the Huang scandal. The New York Times reported on Monday that Nvidia's general counsel, Tim Teter, claimed in emails to Commerce investigators probing Alice Huang's company that he'd been in touch with Jeffrey Kessler, who leads BIS. The Commerce investigation into Megaspeed, which allegedly smuggled restricted chips to China, was then transferred to the Justice Department. By Thursday night, Senate banking committee Chair Tim Scott, R-S.C., summoned both Huang and Lutnick to testify before his committee in December. Later that same night, Lutnick had "proactively agreed to appear voluntarily before the Banking Committee to address their questions," Kristen Eichamer, a Commerce Department spokesperson, said in a statement. Scott threatened to subpoena Huang if he does not appear. A banking panel spokesperson did not immediately respond Friday morning when asked if they'd heard from Huang. "Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive U.S. technology," Scott wrote to Huang. "The American people deserve answers." related.title: Export-banned Nvidia chips are behind China’s most powerful AI models — uh-oh, Jensen!

cards.body: The leading open-weight models developed by Chinese companies were trained on Nvidia chips that the U.S. government restricted from shipping to its largest geopolitical rival, a new research effort claims. The apparently widespread access to Blackwell GPUs among Chinese frontier labs shows the magnitude of the problem facing the leading chip designer. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang left the company this week after admitting to his affair with Alice Huang, executive of Megaspeed, a company implicated in smuggling Nvidia chips into China. Alice Huang has also been alleged to be an agent of China’s intelligence service. While Jensen Huang’s relationships with a customer and two employees have drawn the most public interest, Nvidia’s potential corporate liability for export control violations likely factored into its decision to part ways with Huang. U.S. export controls are intended to protect the country’s leadership in AI capabilities against China, but Huang has long sought to open up that market. Blackwell GPUs are banned from export to China or Chinese-owned firms, while the Trump administration allows Nvidia to export the H200, a less powerful chip, provided shipments take a circuitous shipping route that allows the U.S. to claim a 25% tariff. Will DePue, a former OpenAI researcher who leads the nonprofit research group Unemployment Labs, analyzed the weights — the unique structure — of large language models released openly by DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group. The weights still reflect the configurations of the chips used to train them, and DePue was able to find compelling evidence that the most closely watched models, including Moonshot’s Kimi’s K3 releases and DeepSeek’s V4 models, bear fingerprints from training on Blackwell chips. White House technology adviser Michael Kratsios said earlier this year that Moonshot had used export-banned Nvidia chips, citing U.S. intelligence sources. Epoch AI, a nonprofit research organization, estimates that about two million advanced chips entered China in 2024 and 2025 through schemes designed to hide their final destination. That doesn’t mean that these models were trained entirely on Nvidia chips, or that export control laws were necessarily violated; the chips could have been in an offshore data center, which has proven a popular way for Chinese firms to access compute and driven an industrial revolution in Malaysia. Epoch’s data estimates that 275,000 Nvidia AI accelerators were imported to Malaysia in 2024 and 2025. However, the ostensible goal of the export bans is to prevent exactly that: Chinese AI labs training on the most powerful chips. cards.body: Malaysia and Singapore have intensified scrutiny of AI hardware shipments amid concerns about the potential circumvention of U.S. export restrictions on China. Malaysia has launched an investigation into whether AI hardware imported by a subsidiary of the ill-fated Megaspeed was subsequently exported to other countries, reports Reuters . Meanwhile, Singapore has charged another executive over questionable purchases of 917 servers that may contain Nvidia accelerators, according to The Straits Times . cards.body: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee, as the fallout from ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy intensifies. Lutnick was summoned by Senate Banking Chair Tim Scott amid scrutiny over whether Nvidia could have supplied advanced artificial intelligence chips to Chinese companies and thereby potentially threatened U.S. national security. Huang and Lutnick both received letters on Thursday evening requesting them to testify in separate hearings on Dec. 3 and Dec. 10, respectively. The letter to Lutnick asked the commerce secretary to testify regarding "recent public reports about NVIDIA and the Department of Commerce's role that raises national security concerns." "Secretary Lutnick has proactively agreed to appear voluntarily before the Banking Committee to address their questions," Kristen Eichamer, a spokesperson for Lutnick, told NBC News on Thursday. CNBC contacted the Commerce Department for comment. The letter to Huang said that reports about his relationship with the alleged Chinese spy "raise significant national security concerns." Huang has acknowledged an affair with an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that has bought over $4.8 billion of advanced Nvidia AI chips over the past two years. The scandal, in addition to reports of a separate affair with a senior executive at Nvidia, led to his resignation on Thursday. There is growing bipartisan scrutiny of the Commerce Department Secretary's approach to chip policy and whether his department was doing enough to restrict the supply of AI chips to China. Lawmakers are also questioning whether the department was overseeing Nvidia's exports thoroughly enough Senator Jim Banks has been particularly scathing, saying Lutnick "appears to have used loopholes to allow some of these chip sales to occur," in an appearance on Fox News on Thursday. Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass, who will chair the Senate Banking Committee from January, said on Thursday "Secretary Howard Lutnick and Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler must explain why they have not closed export control loopholes and act today to ensure our advanced technology is not fueling China's military." In a joint letter with incoming Senate Foreign Relations Chair Chris Coons published Wednesday, they said all documents relating to the export of Nvidia chips to China must be preserved. Sen. Ron Wyden, D-Ore. and Rep. Richard E. Neal, D-Mass. told Lutnick they were investigating the approval of sales of Nvidia chips to companies with links to the Chinese government, military and sanctioned entities. Rep. Brian Mast, R-Fla. said on Thursday that Congress needed to investigate the role of the Commerce Department in approving the export to China of AI chips, but added that he had confidence in Lutnick. cards.body: Nvidia co-founder and now former CEO Jensen Huang has never been as prone to controversy as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. But the 63-year-old industry kingpin recently admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in affairs that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and U.S. national security. U.S. officials believe that one of Huang’s likely romantic interests, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.) Megaspeed is a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company that reportedly purchased $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, The New York Times has reported. The story took a sudden turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up. By early Thursday morning, Huang was no longer CEO of the company he co-founded 33 years ago. Then, Thursday afternoon, Reuters dropped another bombshell, publishing a report alleging that Huang had yet another extramarital affair with another unnamed Nvidia employee. The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities. As the controversy unfolds, we are organizing the most relevant events into a reverse-chronological timeline to keep you up to date. cards.body: Singapore, a hub for billions of dollars' worth of Nvidia sales each year, finds itself increasingly in the crosshairs of Washington's push to stop advanced AI chips from reaching China, as the chipmaker CEO's scandal once again thrusts the city-state into the spotlight. The Southeast Asian nation said Thursday that it had barred Alice Huang, the businesswoman at the center of a scandal that catalyzed the end of Jensen Huang's run as Nvidia CEO, from re-entering the country. A fifth person was handed 41 charges on Friday in a Singapore fraud case involving computer servers that might have contained Nvidia chips and were exported to Malaysia. The alleged transactions in the broader case totaled about $390 million, prosecutors said March last year. The investigations into several companies and key officials, including Megaspeed International, began in February 2025 and remained ongoing as of Thursday. Authorities have been examining whether servers exported through Singapore to Malaysia without entering the domestic market were subsequently rerouted to another destination, contrary to declarations made in Singapore, the Ministry of Home Affairs said in a statement late Thursday. Singapore has faced growing international scrutiny, particularly from the U.S., over its role as a major billing and potential transit hub for Nvidia chips that U.S. officials say have reached China. The U.S. has imposed export restrictions on Nvidia's most cutting-edge AI chips to China since 2022 to curb Beijing's surging AI development. Nvidia's revenue linked to Singapore rose to 22% in the fiscal quarter ending July 2025, up from 8% in 2023, with the country's trade ministry estimating chips physically delivered there accounted for less than 1% of the chipmaker's revenue. Singapore at the crossroads? Experts have pointed to gaps in enforcement of U.S. export restrictions and Singapore's corporate system that make it hard to trace where advanced Nvidia chips ultimately end up. Nvidia chips can be legally sold to customers in other countries, such as Malaysia or Singapore, and then illicitly resold or re-exported to China. Chinese companies can also legally gain remote access to the most advanced AI chips hosted in data centers outside China rather than buying the hardware directly. Chris McGuire, a senior fellow at Council on Foreign Relations and former U.S. national security official, said that Southeast Asia has become "a major hub for chip smuggling and export control circumvention," importing tens of billions of dollars' worth of AI chips per year. Singapore has stepped up efforts to police suspected chip diversion since last year, including investigations involving alleged fraud and money laundering. Authorities acknowledged the potential "blind spots between separate monitoring of trade flows and banking flows," said Alvin Camba, lead scientist and director of research at Lyvi, an Austin-based AI risk assessment firm. cards.body: I was the last person at CNBC to do a live broadcast interview with Jensen Huang. At the time, Huang still seemed untouchable. But weeks later, Nvidia is confronting a question investors hadn't had to confront in more than 30 years: What does the company look like without him? I sat down with the company founder on Oct. 22 at Nvidia's GTC event in Berlin, Germany, just weeks before he admitted to an affair with a woman that U.S. intelligence alleges could be a spy for China. "Jensenmania," as I like to call it — which had come to characterize the CEO's appearances — was in full force at the Berlin event. The Nvidia merchandise store featured clothing with Huang's face on it, huge cheers erupted when he appeared on stage, and attendees were doing their best to secure a picture with the Nvidia founder. Huang had somewhat of a rockstar persona with a fandom to match in every city he visited around the world. In 2025, I followed Huang around on his visit to Europe. At an event in London, an attendee who was eagerly waiting to catch a glimpse of Huang compared the Nvidia boss to "Iron Man," referencing the popular character of the Marvel superhero and tech billionaire inventor Tony Stark. These moments that I experienced really embodied what Huang had become – a larger-than-life personality who was central to the excitement around artificial intelligence. Less CEO, more AI hype man, evangelical about the technology and its transformative power. He had the credentials to back it up. Since he co-founded Nvidia in the early 90s, Huang helped shape the company from a startup taking on incumbents to a dominant player for AI chips. Over the last three decades, he saw the shifts coming, investing to turn what were initially chips designed for rendering gaming graphics – GPUs – into general-purpose AI computing semiconductors, along with the software that gave Nvidia its strong position. Huang's AI vision The near 500% rally in Nvidia's shares over the past five years has been driven by its incredible growth, but also the backing of Huang's vision. "Nvidia without Jensen is something which we've never really considered," Storm Uru, co-head of the global innovation team at Liontrust Asset Management, which has been invested in Nvidia since 2017, told me. Now it is a reality. Huang is out and he has left some of the biggest shoes to fill in tech history – without a clear succession plan in place. cards.body: Nvidia investors turned bearish before this week's Jensen Huang saga. But the selling on Wall Street accelerated in the past few days, sending the stock to its sixth straight weekly drop, the longest losing streak since 2012. The chip giant, which spent most of the year as the world's most valuable company, has lost 30% of its value during the losing streak. That's a drop of roughly $1.7 trillion in market cap and it pushed the company below Apple. Huang, who co-founded Nvidia and led it for 33 years, resigned on Thursday after two separate extramarital affairs — one with an alleged Chinese spy and the other with an employee — were made public. The board named finance chief Colette Kress as interim CEO while it conducts a search for a full-time successor. Nvidia shares fell 13% this week, the most since April 2025. News of the first reported affair hit the front pages over the weekend, when Huang sent a letter to employees apologizing for being "unfaithful to my wife." The board convened late Wednesday after The New York Times reported on the other affair, this one with the company's vice president of health care. By early Thursday morning, Huang was out, capping a stunning fall for the Nvidia co-founder, who had emerged as one of President Donald Trump's top allies in the corporate world. "With the unfortunate departure of CEO Jensen Huang we expect a challenging transition for NVIDIA over the next few months," Gil Luria, an analyst at D.A. Davidson, wrote in a report on Thursday. Luria lowered his price target to $200 from $300, but maintained his buy rating. "We believe the market has appropriately adjusted for this transition," he wrote. Last week, prior to Huang's departure, Nvidia shares dropped about 9%. Much of the decline came after the midterm elections, which resulted in sweeping victories for Democrats and the passage of dozens of ballot measures that could slow the artificial intelligence buildout. In the weeks before the election, Nvidia's stock was sliding alongside the rest of the AI trade on concerns that rising interest rates would punish debt-heavy companies. While Nvidia is wildly profitable, big customers like neoclouds are reliant on the debt markets. Heading into next week, the pressure is on Kress. Nvidia is scheduled to report quarterly results on Tuesday. Analysts are projecting 91% year-over-year revenue growth to $108.9 billion, according to LSEG. That's up 18-fold from the same quarter in 2022, just before OpenAI launched ChatGPT and kicked off the generative AI era. Analysts at Oppenheimer wrote in a report on Thursday that, even though they see the company reporting solid earnings, "we expect fundamentals to take a backseat near term." "The departure of Mr. Huang could, in our view, translate to a lingering share overhang," they wrote. WATCH: Sell rating on Nvidia

cards.body: 젠슨 황 엔비디아 전 최고경영자(CEO) 퇴진 영향으로 그가 주도했던 5000억달러(약 670조원) 규모 d인공지능(AI) 산업 금융 지원 구상이 흔들리기 시작했다. 미국 뉴욕타임스(NYT)는 13일(현지시간) 해당 구상 관계자 3명을 인용, 금융지원 계획이 현재 유동적인 상황이라고 보도했다. 특히 당초 참여하기로 했던 금융기관 6곳 가운데 최소 1곳이 전날 참여 철회를 논의한 것으로 알려졌다. 황 전 CEO는 지난 8월 아폴로 글로벌 매니지먼트·블랙록·블랙스톤·브룩필드 자산운용·골드만삭스·KKR 등 6개 금융회사 경영진과 함께 총 5000억달러 규모의 AI 컴퓨팅 관련 거래에 자금을 공급하겠다는 목표를 공개했다. 해당 구상은 황 전 CEO가 AI 기업들이 고가의 반도체를 구매하는 데 필요한 자금을 조달하도록 월가 대형 금융기관들을 규합하면서 추진됐다. 아직까지는 실행된 대출은 없는 것으로 전해졌다. 일부 금융회사 내부에서도 해당 구상을 알지 못하는 상황이었다고 NYT는 전했다. 이 계획은 황 전 CEO의 퇴진 이전부터 금융 보증 조건을 둘러싼 이견으로 추진에 난항이 있었던 것으로 나타났다. 블룸버그 통신은 이날 엔비디아가 지난 한 달간 일부 고객사와 월가 협력사들로부터 금융 보증 규모를 확대하라는 요구를 받아왔다고 보도했다. 황 전 CEO는 이 같은 금융지원 구상 외에도 AI 산업 관련 대규모 투자와 금융거래를 주도해왔다. 코어위브와 네비우스, 아이렌 등 데이터센터 기업의 지분을 확보했으며, AI 반도체 및 관련 기술 기업에 대한 투자와 인수도 추진했다. 마이클 에드워즈 AI 전문 투자은행 포럼마켓츠 이사는 “엔비디아는 AI 산업의 중앙은행”이라며 “의장이 없는 연방준비제도(Fed)를 상상해보라”고 말했다. 한편 엔비디아가 글로벌 AI 반도체 공급에서 여전히 막강한 영향력을 갖고 있고 풍부한 현금도 보유하고 있어 근본적 위상은 건재하다는 의견도 있다. 트럼프 행정부도 AI 산업의 규제 관련 의제에 우호적이라는 점에서 이 같은 견해에 힘을 보태고 있다. 권동준 기자 djkwon@etnews.com - 권동준 기자기사 더보기 - ET Events

headlines.body: Leading semiconductor research firm SemiAnalysis believes that Jensen Huang's sudden departure from Nvidia may have been driven not only by revelations about his personal extramarital relationships, but also by widespread illicit exports of advanced AI accelerators to China. In its latest newsletter, analysts estimate that more than 1.5 gigawatts (GW) worth of restricted Nvidia hardware, which could be equivalent to up to 1.5 million GPUs, has reached the country despite U.S. export controls. The estimate excludes processors that Nvidia specifically developed to comply with U.S. export rules, such as the H20 or H800. The firm also claims that the U.S. Department of Commerce has reached a similar conclusion about the scale of unauthorized shipments. Yet, SemiAnalysis does not disclose the exact number of accelerators shipped to China illegally, or their split between Nvidia's product generations. The scale of the alleged diversions is particularly notable because modern AI accelerators require substantial power and infrastructure. While the report does not explain how it converts accelerator quantities into power figures, it is likely that the company uses package-level nameplate/rated power multiplied by the number of GPUs. Assuming that all of these AI GPUs were Nvidia H200 SXM rated for up to 700W, then China got around 2.142 million of such accelerators, while if all of these processors were B200 SXM rated for up to 1,000W, then we are talking about 1.5 million units. For a mixed deployment, the total would fall between these figures, depending on the proportion of H200 and B200 accelerators. To put these numbers into context, xAI's Colossus One had 220-230,000 Hopper H100 and H200 GPUs, whereas the Colossus 2 has a target of 1.2 million Blackwell B200 and B300 GPUs. That said, 1.5 GW of restricted Nvidia hardware in China represents an enormous amount of computing infrastructure, which is comparable, or even exceeds, the scale of xAI's entire existing Colossus operation. While SemiAnalysis did not reveal all the cases in which restricted AI accelerators reached the People's Republic of China, it supports its assessment with two well-known cases of alleged GPU smuggling. headlines.body: In late September, Cantor Fitzgerald hosted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and other top executives from the chipmaker for investor meetings in New York, according to a Cantor research report reviewed by CNBC. The Wall Street firm liked what it heard. "We continue to view NVDA as the best risk/reward in our coverage," Cantor analyst C.J. Muse and his colleagues wrote in a research report dated Oct. 3 that maintained a $350 price target and overweight rating on the stock. Yet the firm, formerly run by Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and now led by his sons, Brandon and Kyle, reported a nearly 50% decline in the number of Nvidia shares it held between September 2025 and March 2026, according to a CNBC analysis of securities filings that excludes options. Nvidia had been one of the largest stock positions reported in Cantor's filings. The decline coincided with White House and U.S. intelligence officials pressing Lutnick to crack down on Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company suspected of funneling Nvidia's advanced artificial intelligence chips to China. Lutnick repeatedly resisted those efforts, Axios reported Nov. 11. By the time Cantor hosted Huang in New York, Lutnick had also received a classified intelligence warning, according to a Nov. 10 Axios report, about Huang's ties to a suspected Chinese spy and had appeared alongside the CEO at a G20 technology summit in North Carolina. Even as Cantor pared back its Nvidia stake, it continued doing business across the chipmaker's AI empire. A CNBC review of securities filings, corporate announcements and Wall Street research found the firm has helped arrange billions of dollars in financing for Nvidia's business partners while maintaining close ties to the chipmaker's leadership. Those ties have drawn fresh scrutiny following Huang's resignation Thursday and Axios' reporting that Lutnick repeatedly resisted a crackdown on companies suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips to China, despite President Donald Trump authorizing new export restrictions on those companies for a third time on Nov. 5. An ethics expert said the relationship between Lutnick and his former firm's investments may raise questions, given what the secretary knew about Nvidia. Richard Painter, the former chief White House ethics lawyer for President George W. Bush and now a corporate law professor at the University of Minnesota, said that while "there's no proof of" Lutnick sharing nonpublic information with Cantor Fitzgerald, "the appearance doesn't look great." "His conversations with his sons better be about publicly available information," Painter told CNBC. There is no evidence that Lutnick's sons had advance knowledge of the intelligence concerns, that changes in Cantor's reported holdings were tied to any warnings or that the firm's business interests influenced their father's decisions. headlines.body: It was the resignation heard across the world. Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s embattled CEO who co-founded and led the company for 33 years, had officially stepped down. “It’s like a bomb went off,” one neocloud founder told TechCrunch when he first heard the news. Over the last several years, Nvidia has been a prolific investor, pouring tens of billions into startups annually and participating in 105 rounds this year alone, often as the largest investor, according to PitchBook. “If that direction changes, it’ll be a big blow to so many young companies,” said Maria Davidson, founder of Relational Capital. Huang’s absence leaves the startup ecosystem without one of its biggest champions and with far less capital for now, investors say, which could have a massive impact on dealmaking, valuations, funding, and even competition. “Nvidia is carrying almost every AI-native startup from application to neocloud,” Dawn Capital’s Shamillah Bankiya told TechCrunch. Most of the significant decisions to invest in startups often came from Jensen himself, according to Umesh Padval, managing partner at Seligman Ventures. Padval has known Huang since serving on the board of Mellanox Technologies, a networking chipmaker Nvidia acquired for approximately $7 billion in 2020. While there is hope that Huang’s eventual successor will resume his dealmaking spree, investors aren’t hopeful that it will happen in the short term. Nvidia’s interim CEO, Colette Kress, is expected to institute some changes, especially when it comes to Nvidia’s investments into AI startups at the crux of the billion-dollar data center build-out. Huang’s rampant dealmaking in this sphere has been a source of concern for Wall Street. “She’s much more conservative,” one investor said of Kress. “I don’t think she’s going to commit the same amount of money to keep the early-stage ecosystem going.” Nvidia’s biggest bets were backing neoclouds, inference providers, and open weight models, which are expensive for smaller companies to build. “Jensen’s initiatives are a big reason an ecosystem has emerged despite that,” Zain Javaid, co-founder of the hardware company Ghost, said. For instance, Nvidia backed CoreWeave when it was still private and participated in two of Crusoe’s rounds, including its $1.4 billion Series E. headlines.body: Nvidia is facing one the biggest crises in its 33 year history, with founder Jensen Huang resigning as CEO Thursday after multiple reported affairs, including one with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy. Now CFO Colette Kress has taken the helm as Nvidia's interim CEO. The implications of Huang's affair with Alice Huang run far deeper than infidelity. That's because her ties to Nvidia customer Megaspeed put her in the middle of a sprawling effort to accumulate AI chips across Southeast Asia. And Megaspeed is under investigation for possibly diverting restricted Nvidia chips into the hands of Chinese companies. The relationship between Jensen Huang and Alice Huang dates back to 2023, according to The New York Times. That was a "turbulent" period for Nvidia, Jensen Huang told CNBC during an interview at the time. Nvidia was in the midst of redesigning some chips to comply with the first in a series of strict export controls imposed by the U.S. government that restricted sales to China. "The regulation is going to be just fine. We're going to be able to work through it," Huang told CNBC from Nvidia's headquarters in February 2023. The interview was for a documentary about how Huang created Nvidia and built it into the backbone of the AI boom. That same day, CNBC also interviewed Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare, with whom Jensen Huang reportedly had an affair. It's not the first time Nvidia has faced an uncertain future. The company nearly went bankrupt in the early years after it was founded in 1993. "Every company makes mistakes and I make a lot of them," Huang said in the 2023 interview. "And some of them put the company in peril." In the early months of the AI boom, after OpenAI launched ChatGPT in November 2022, Nvidia was on the precipice of historic growth. Jensen Huang told CNBC he'd like to keep running the company for "three or four decades," as long as "I feel that I'm making a real contribution to the company." Less than four years later, Jensen Huang is out, and we're taking a look back at our interviews with the Nvidia co-founder and other company executives as the chipmaker enters this next critical chapter. headlines.body: AI 추천 뉴스 "HBM 없는 AI 추론…열 빼기 쉬운 적층 구조가 해법" 시드 세스 디매트릭스 CEO 삼전닉스 투자받은 美스타트업 메모리·연산 결합한 AI칩 개발 “앞으로 5년 간 가장 중요한 기술은 메모리와 연산장치를 함께 묶는 첨단 패키징입니다.” 시드 세스 디매트릭스(D-Matrix) 최고경영자(CEO·사진)는 지난 10일(현지시간) 미국 샌타클래라 본사에서 기자와 만나 이같이 말했다. 빅테크가 고대역폭메모리(HBM)를 모으는 사이 스타트업 디매트릭스는 전혀 다른 해법을 모색하고 있었다. HBM을 쓰지 않는 AI칩으로 추론 시장을 공략하겠다는 것이다. 2019년 설립된 디매트릭스는 추론(AI가 작업을 수행하는 과정)용 반도체를 개발하는 스타트업이다. 지난해 시리즈C 투자 유치 때 기업가치 20억달러(약 2조6700억원)를 인정받았다. SK하이닉스와 삼성벤처투자가 각각 시리즈A·B 투자에 참여했다. 세스 CEO는 “초기 투자자인 SK하이닉스는 장기적으로 추론에 새로운 메모리 구조가 필요하다는 문제의식에 공감했다”고 했다. 디매트릭스의 주력 제품은 추론용 칩 ‘커세어’다. 반도체 내 고속 메모리인 정적램(SRAM)을 중심으로 메모리와 연산부를 가깝게 배치해 데이터 이동시간과 전력효율을 높였다. 지난 9월에는 차세대 반도체인 ‘랩터’를 엔비디아의 네트워크 플랫폼 NV링크 퓨전과 MGX 랙에 통합하는 파트너십을 발표했다. 내년 4분기 출시를 목표로 개발 중인 ‘랩터’는 D램을 아래에, 연산장치를 위에 쌓는다. 연산장치 위에 메모리를 올리는 삼성전자의 ‘zHBM’과 위아래 배치가 반대다. 세스 CEO는 “연산장치가 위에 있으면 열을 빼내기 쉽다”며 “이미 확보한 패키징 기술을 활용해 제품을 더 빨리 내놓을 수 있다”고 설명했다. 세스 CEO는 미 중간선거 결과 데이터센터 건설이 지연되면 자사 반도체 가치가 더욱 높아질 것으로 봤다. 엔비디아 호퍼 등 구형 그래픽처리장치(GPU)에 자사 제품을 결합하면 성능을 1.5~2배 높이고 교체 시기를 늦출 수 있어서다. 실리콘밸리=김인엽 특파원 inside@hankyung.com

summary_data.korean_title: NVIDIA SOMA Retargeter, 인간 동작을 로봇에 맞게 변환하는 기술 공개
summary_data.korean_summary: NVIDIA가 인간의 동작 데이터를 휴머노이드 로봇의 신체 구조에 맞게 변환하는 SOMA Retargeter를 기술 블로그를 통해 소개했다.

action.action: 인간 동작 데이터를 로봇의 관절 구조·가동범위에 맞게 재변환(retarget)하는 SOMA Retargeter 기술 소개
action.scope: 휴머노이드 로봇 전반, 구체적 제품·고객 미확인

key_facts: **인간 동작 시연은 자연스러운 움직임의 조정과 타이밍을 포착**하는 좋은 학습 출발점으로 제시됨
로봇은 인체와 **신체 비율, 관절 구조, 가동 범위가 다르기 때문**에 인간 동작을 그대로 복제할 수 없음
따라서 동작을 로봇에 맞게 적응(retarget)시키는 과정이 필요하다고 설명
본문은 NVIDIA Technical Blog에 게재된 소개 글로, 구체적 수치·출시일·고객사 미확인
summary_data.why_matters: **휴머노이드 로봇 학습 데이터 파이프라인에서 모션 리타겟팅은 핵심 병목**으로, 인간 시연 데이터를 다양한 로봇 폼팩터에 재사용 가능하게 만드는 기술은 학습 효율성과 범용성을 좌우한다. 이는 로봇 개발사들이 개별 로봇마다 새로 데이터를 수집할 필요를 줄여 개발 속도와 비용 구조에 직접 영향을 미친다.
summary_data.subject_angle: NVIDIA가 **휴머노이드 로봇 학습용 소프트웨어 스택(시뮬레이션·데이터 생성·리타겟팅)으로 영역을 확장**하고 있음을 보여주며, 하드웨어가 아닌 로봇 개발의 데이터·툴 계층에서 플랫폼 지위를 강화하려는 전략의 일환으로 해석된다.
summary_data.focus_angle: 자동차·휴머노이드 로봇 OEM 입장에서는 **인간 시연 데이터를 다양한 로봇 바디에 재사용할 수 있게 하는 리타겟팅 도구가 휴머노이드 작업 숙련 학습의 비용을 낮춰**, 공장 자동화나 조립 라인 투입 휴머노이드 개발 속도를 가속할 수 있는 요소로 작용한다.

summary_data.korean_title: NVIDIA, Jetson AGX Orin용 DLA 파이썬 네이티브 추론 지원 - cuDLA 활용법 공개
summary_data.korean_summary: NVIDIA가 엣지 디바이스 개발자를 위해 Jetson AGX Orin의 DLA(Deep Learning Accelerator)를 cuDLA API로 파이썬에서 네이티브로 제어할 수 있는 방법을 기술 블로그로 공개했다.

action.action: Jetson AGX Orin에서 cuDLA를 이용한 Python 기반 DLA 네이티브 추론 실행 방법을 기술 문서로 공개
action.scope: NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, DLA 플랫폼, Python 개발 환경

key_facts: **NVIDIA DLA(Deep Learning Accelerator)는 딥러닝 추론을 위한 전용 하드웨어 플랫폼**
Jetson AGX Orin에서 DLA는 지원되는 신경망 연산을 실행하여 GPU의 추론 작업을 오프로드 가능
엣지 AI 애플리케이션은 제한된 컴퓨팅·전력 예산 내에서 다수의 신경망을 동시 실행해야 하는 요구가 있음
DLA 오프로드를 통해 전력 효율성 개선 및 GPU 자원 확보가 가능함
summary_data.why_matters: **엣지 AI에서 전력·연산 자원 제약은 자율주행·로봇 등 실시간 추론 시스템의 핵심 병목**이며, DLA를 통한 GPU 오프로드는 동시 다중 모델 실행 요구를 충족하는 데 중요하다. Python 네이티브 지원은 개발 편의성을 높여 Jetson 플랫폼 기반 엣지 AI 생태계 확장에 기여한다.
summary_data.subject_angle: **NVIDIA는 Jetson Orin 플랫폼의 전용 가속기(DLA) 활용성을 높여 GPU+DLA 이종 컴퓨팅 전략을 강화**하고, 개발자 접근성 개선을 통해 엣지 AI·로보틱스 생태계에서의 플랫폼 종속성을 공고히 하려는 전략으로 해석된다.
summary_data.focus_angle: DLA를 통한 GPU 오프로드는 자율주행차·휴머노이드 로봇에서 카메라·센서 기반 다중 신경망(인식, 추적 등)을 동시에 저전력으로 처리해야 하는 OEM·로봇 개발사에 직접적인 실익을 제공하며, Jetson AGX Orin이 이러한 온보드 멀티태스크 추론의 표준 플랫폼으로 자리잡는 데 기여한다.

headlines.body: 일론 머스크 테슬라 최고경영자(CEO)의 입방정이 최근 세간에 화제를 모았다. 혼외관계 논란과 중국 정보기관 연계 의혹의 중심에 있는 엔비디아의 젠슨 황 전 CEO를 영입하고 싶다고 언급한 것이다. 이처럼 머스크는 그간 소셜미디어(SNS)와 공식 석상에서 내놓은 말로 시장을 흔들고 논란을 일으켜 왔다. 저가형 전기차 개발부터 사이버트럭 판매 전망, 자율주행 상용화까지 그가 내놓은 장밋빛 전망은 시장의 기대를 키웠지만, 실제 결과는 당초 발언과 차이를 보인 경우가 적지 않다. 머스크는 2017년 차세대 로드스터를 공개하면서 2020년 고객에게 인도하겠다고 밝혔다. 당시 공개된 로드스터는 정지 상태에서 시속 60마일(약 97㎞)까지 1.9초 만에 도달하고, 한 번 충전으로 약 1000㎞를 주행할 수 있도록 설계됐다. 그러나 약속한 시점에 차량은 출시되지 않았다. 머스크는 2021년 공급망 문제를 이유로 인도 시점을 2023년으로 미뤘다. 이후에도 일정은 여러 차례 연기됐다. 결국 지난달이 되어서야 신형 로드스터를 공개하면서 2028년 생산을 시작하겠다고 밝혔다. 최초 인도 목표보다 8년 늦어진 일정이다. 2018년에는 테슬라 비상장 전환을 둘러싼 발언으로 주식시장을 흔들었다. 머스크는 그해 8월 7일 트위터(현 X)에 “테슬라를 주당 420달러(약 52만원)에 비상장사로 전환하는 방안을 고려하고 있다. 자금은 확보했다”고 게시했다. 당시 테슬라 주가는 당일 종가 기준 10.98% 급등했다. 머스크의 발언으로 미국 증권거래위원회(SEC)는 실제 자금 조달이 확정되지 않았는데도 투자자를 오도했다며 증권 사기 혐의를 제기했다. 머스크는 사우디아라비아 국부펀드와의 논의를 근거로 자금이 확보됐다고 판단했다고 해명했지만, 결국 17일 만에 비상장 전환 계획을 철회했다. 머스크는 트위터에 게시한 글 한 문장 때문에 테슬라와 각각 2000만달러(약 266억8000만원)의 벌금을 내게 됐다. 이후 머스크는 이사회 의장직에서도 물러났고, 테슬라 관련 주요 SNS 게시물에 대해 사전 검토받는 절차도 마련됐다. 자율주행 기술에 대한 전망 역시 실제 일정과 차이를 보였다. 머스크는 2019년 4월 자율주행 기술 행사에서 “내년이면 100만대 이상의 로보택시가 도로를 달릴 것”이라고 말했다. 테슬라 차량 소유자가 차를 차량 공유 서비스에 등록하면 운전자 없이 승객을 태우고 수익을 얻을 수 있다는 구상이었다. 그러나 2020년까지 대규모 무인 로보택시 서비스는 실현되지 않았다. 머스크는 발언 두 달 뒤 주주총회에서 100만대의 자율주행 가능 차량을 확보하겠다는 취지로 설명을 바꿨다. 테슬라의 완전자율주행(FSD) 기능도 상용화 목표 시점이 여러 차례 늦춰졌다. 머스크는 대중들에게 저가형 전기차 시대의 꿈을 심어주기도 했다. 그는 2020년 배터리 데이 행사에서 “3년 뒤 2만5000달러(약 3334만원)짜리 전기차를 만들 수 있을 것”이라고 밝혔다. 배터리 생산 비용을 낮춰 전기차 가격을 대폭 낮추겠다는 구상이었다. 그의 말과 달리 저가형 전기차는 나오지 않았다. 로이터통신은 2024년 테슬라가 일반 운전자가 이용하는 저가형 전기차 개발을 중단하고 로보택시에 집중하기로 했다고 보도했다. 머스크는 당시 보도를 부인했지만, 같은 해 실적 발표에서 3000만원대 저가형 전기차를 만드는 건 의미가 없다는 취지로 말했다. 사이버트럭에 대한 의지를 드러낸 적도 있다. 그는 2023년 테슬라 주주총회에서 전기 픽업트럭인 사이버트럭의 연간 판매량이 "25만대에서 50만대까지 가능하다"고 전망했다. 그의 자신감과 달리 사이버트럭은 판매실적이 저조했다. 미국 자동차 시장조사업체 켈리블루북에 따르면 사이버트럭의 2025년 미국 판매량은 2만237대로 전년 대비 48% 감소했다. 머스크가 제시했던 목표치의 약 20분의 1 수준이다. 글로벌 누적 판매량도 7만대 수준에 불과한 것으로 추산됐다. 테슬라는 예상과 달리 판매량이 저조하자 사이버트럭 생산을 2027년 중반께 정리하고 해당 생산 역량을 로보택시 사이버캡에 투입하겠다는 계획을 밝혔다. 허인학 기자 ih.heo@chosunbiz.com
